ai.text:
The Modernizing Access to Our Public Oceans Act tells the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to create standard, public map-based information about where people can boat and fish in federal waters.

NOAA must work with state and local governments, Indian tribes, Native Hawaiian organizations, and other interested groups to set standards for gathering and sharing this location data. The data covers fishing restrictions and where certain recreational boats may go in federal waters, including the exclusive economic zone of the United States. That zone generally covers waters from 3 to 200 miles out from the U.S. coast.

Within four years of the act becoming law, NOAA must publish this information on a public website. The website must show where fishing is restricted and under what conditions, which areas of the exclusive economic zone limit certain types of recreational boats, and which places are federally protected, such as National Marine Sanctuaries. NOAA must also keep sharing digital navigation information about that zone on the site, as far as is practical.

The act lets NOAA partner with outside groups to carry this out. It also requires NOAA to work with other federal agencies so their databases are compatible and can share recreational ocean-use data smoothly.

summary.text:
Modernizing Access to Our Public Oceans Act
This act directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to standardize and publish geospatial data related to public recreational use of federal waterways (e.g., boating and fishing).
Under the act, NOAA must consult with relevant stakeholders (including state and local governments, Indian tribes, and Native Hawaiian organizations) to develop and adopt standards for the coordination and dissemination of geospatial data relating to fishing restrictions and recreational vessels' use of federal waterways, including the exclusive economic zone of the United States (EEZ). (The EEZ generally includes waters between 3 and 200 miles seaward from the U.S. coastline.)
Within four years after the act is enacted, NOAA must provide geographic information system data on a public website that identifies and describes the locations where and conditions under which certain recreational activities are restricted in federal waterways. Specifically, the website must identify (1) locations where fishing restrictions are imposed, (2) areas in the EEZ with restrictions on specified recreational vessel types, and (3) federally protected areas (e.g., National Marine Sanctuaries). NOAA must also continue to provide digitized navigation information related to the EEZ and make the information available on the website to the extent practicable.
The act allows NOAA to coordinate and partner with nonfederal entities to carry out this act. It also directs NOAA to work with other federal agencies to ensure compatibility and interoperability among federal databases with respect to collecting and disseminating geospatial data related to the public outdoor recreational use of the EEZ.
